items.prompt: Why does a polar bear have thick fur and a layer of fat?

options.text: to help it swim faster
options.why: Fur and fat are for warmth.

options.text: to stay warm in the cold
to hide from the Sun
options.why: There is little sun in its habitat.

hints: Polar bears live in very cold places.
Fur and fat are like a thick coat.
items.explanation: Thick fur and fat keep a polar bear warm in freezing places.

items.prompt: Which feature helps a cactus survive in a desert?

options.text: big thin leaves
options.why: Big leaves would lose too much water.

options.text: a thick stem that stores water
shallow roots that never spread
options.why: Cactus roots spread wide to catch rain.

hints: A cactus needs to keep water.
items.explanation: A cactus stores water in its thick stem and has small spiny leaves that lose little water.

items.prompt: A feature that helps a living thing survive in its habitat is called an ___.
hints: It is a long word with ten letters.
items.explanation: An adaptation helps a living thing survive in its habitat.

items.prompt: Why do rainforest plants often have leaves with pointed tips?

options.text: to catch more sunlight
options.why: The tips are for letting water run off.

options.text: to let rain drip off quickly
to keep animals away
options.why: The tips are mainly for water.

hints: Too much water can harm leaves.
items.explanation: Pointed tips let rainwater drip off, so the leaves do not stay too wet.

items.prompt: A camel has wide, flat feet. How does this help it?

options.text: It helps the camel swim.
options.why: Camels do not swim.

options.text: It stops the camel from sinking into soft sand.
It keeps the camel warm.
options.why: Flat feet do not keep it warm.

items.explanation: Wide feet spread the camel's weight, so it does not sink into soft sand.

items.prompt: Which feature of a flower helps attract insects?

options.text: sharp thorns
options.why: Thorns do not attract insects.

options.text: bright petals and sweet nectar
green leaves
options.why: Leaves are for making food.

hints: Bright colours are easy to see.
items.explanation: Bright petals and nectar attract insects, which can then carry pollen.

items.prompt: Why do many animals in cold places have thick fur?

options.text: to run faster
options.why: Fur is for warmth.

options.text: to trap heat close to the body
to look big
options.why: Fur does not help them look big in the way heat is kept.

hints: The air in fur is a good insulator.
items.explanation: Thick fur traps a layer of warm air close to the body.

items.prompt: Sort each adaptation into the habitat where it helps most.

items.text: stores water in a thick stem
can go a long time without drinking
thick fur and a layer of fat

hints: Think about what each habitat is like.
items.explanation: Water stores help in dry places, fur and fat help in the cold, and pointed leaf tips help in wet places.

items.prompt: How does a light, fluffy seed help a plant?

options.text: It makes the seed grow faster.
options.why: The fluff helps with travel.

options.text: It can be carried far away by the wind.
It makes the seed taste sweet.
options.why: Fluff does not change taste.

hints: Seeds need to move away from the parent plant.
Light things float in the air.
items.explanation: Light, fluffy seeds are blown by the wind to new places, where they can grow without crowding the parent plant.

items.prompt: A burdock plant has seeds with tiny hooks. How do the hooks help?

options.text: They stop animals from eating the plant.
options.why: The hooks help spread the seeds.

options.text: They catch on animal fur and are carried away.
They help the seeds float in water.
options.why: Hooks are for sticking to things.

hints: Seeds need to spread to new places.
Hooks stick to things that brush past.
items.explanation: Hooked seeds stick to animals and are carried to new places.

items.prompt: Why is it helpful for plants to spread their seeds?

options.text: Seeds grow faster in the dark.
options.why: Most seeds need water and later light.

options.text: Seeds far from the parent plant have more space, light and water.
The parent plant dies when seeds fall near it.
options.why: This is not always so. The seeds simply compete.

hints: Think about plants growing close together.
items.explanation: Spread seeds do not have to compete with the parent plant for light, water and space.

items.prompt: Which feature helps a predator catch its prey?

options.text: eyes on the sides of the head
options.why: Side eyes are common in prey animals.

options.text: sharp claws and forward-facing eyes
a very long tail only
options.why: A tail alone does not catch prey.

hints: Claws help to grab and hold.
items.explanation: Predators often have sharp teeth or claws and forward-facing eyes to judge distance.

items.prompt: Why do many prey animals, such as rabbits, have eyes on the sides of their heads?

options.text: to see better in the dark only
options.why: Side eyes give a wide view.

options.text: to see danger from nearly all directions
to look bigger
options.why: They give a wide view.

hints: Prey animals need to spot predators.
A wide view means fewer surprises.
Think of eyes at the front versus the side.
items.explanation: Side-facing eyes give a very wide view, so prey can spot predators early.

items.prompt: Which features help prey animals avoid being caught?

options.text: forward-facing eyes for judging distance
options.why: These help predators.

options.text: camouflage that matches their surroundings
fast legs for running away
sharp claws for hunting
options.why: These help predators.

hints: Prey want to stay hidden or escape.
Predators use claws and forward-facing eyes.
items.explanation: Camouflage and speed help prey escape. Claws and forward-facing eyes help predators.

items.prompt: An animal that is hunted by another animal is called ___.
hints: It is the opposite of predator.
items.explanation: The hunted animal is the prey.

items.prompt: A fennec fox lives in the desert and has very large ears. How might this help it?

options.text: The ears keep it warm.
options.why: In a hot place the ears help it lose heat.

options.text: Heat can leave its body through the large ears to keep it cool.
The ears store water.
options.why: Ears do not store water.

hints: Large ears have a large surface.
Heat can escape from a large surface.
items.explanation: Large ears give a big surface, so the fox can lose heat and stay cool.

items.prompt: An arctic hare has white fur in winter. What is the main advantage?

options.text: It makes the hare warmer than brown fur would.
options.why: The main advantage is camouflage.

options.text: It is camouflaged against the snow.
It lets the hare see in the dark.
options.why: Fur colour does not change eyesight.

hints: Think about what colour snow is.
items.explanation: White fur helps the hare hide against the snow from predators.

items.prompt: A water lily has leaves that float on the surface. How does this help the plant?

options.text: The leaves can store more water.
options.why: The plant already has plenty of water.

options.text: The leaves can reach sunlight above the water.
The leaves can catch insects.
options.why: This is not a water lily feature.

hints: Plants need light to make food.
Light is brightest at the surface.
items.explanation: Floating leaves lie at the surface, where they get the most sunlight.

items.prompt: A desert plant has very small leaves or spines. Which is the best reason?

options.text: Small leaves catch more sunlight.
options.why: Small leaves catch less sunlight.

options.text: Less surface means less water is lost.
Spines make the plant tastier.
options.why: Spines are not for taste.

items.explanation: Small leaves or spines have a small surface, so they lose less water.

items.prompt: Why are animals suited to one habitat often unable to live well in another?

options.text: They forget how to live elsewhere.
options.why: It is about body features, not memory.

options.text: Their adaptations help in their own habitat but may not help elsewhere.
All habitats are exactly the same.
options.why: Habitats differ a lot.

hints: A polar bear in the desert would overheat.
Adaptations are linked to a habitat.
items.explanation: An adaptation that helps in one habitat, like thick fur, may be harmful in another.

items.prompt: A flower is pollinated by wind, not insects. Which feature would you expect?

options.text: large bright petals and sweet nectar
options.why: These attract insects.

options.text: small dull petals and lots of light pollen
a strong sweet smell
options.why: Wind does not smell anything.

hints: Wind does not need to be attracted.
Insect flowers are big and bright.
items.explanation: Wind-pollinated flowers are usually small and dull, with plenty of light pollen the wind can carry.
